title: Post-loop residue: infra candidate (Samir Banerjee)
content:
Quick dump from the 1:1 loop with Samir Banerjee — informal, messy, want to capture the vibes + concrete open flags before the panel converges. Do not treat this as polished feedback; will refine after sync with Marco.

Context / setup:
- Role: Senior Infrastructure Engineer (inference infra — autoscaling/batching)
- Loop format: 45m system-design + 30m coding + 15m behavioral followups (me + Marco + Priya)
- Candidate came in with a recent background at a mid-size infra startup; worked on autoscalers and KV-cache mechanics.

Raw timeline notes (timestamps approximate):
- 0–10m: quick intro, Samir very direct, uses specific anecdotes ("we lost 3% QPS after switching to async rebalancer"). Good signal of operational ownership.
- 10–35m: system design prompt (scalable KV cache with cross-region read-through and stale-reads policy).
  - Thought process: started with requirements, called out tradeoffs between consistency and latency, proposed hybrid approach (local LRU + global consensus for leases).
  - Positive: quantified numbers (target p99 < 60ms, target consistency window <= 200ms), sketched eviction/rehit metrics to drive autoscaler.
  - Concern: leaned heavily on Paxos-style lease mechanism but glossed over how partition tolerance would behave under network flaps (didn't tie to concrete mitigation like vectored heartbeats or circuit-breaker windows).
- 35–65m: coding exercise (simplified batching simulation + failure injection).
  - Implemented a clean event loop and used backpressure tokens; code was readable but missing a couple of defensive checks (null/timeout edge cases).
  - Debugging: when I injected node delay, he suggested graceful degradation (read-only mode) but didn't fully trace how KV cache invalidation would propagate.
- 65–80m: behavioral / collaboration questions.
  - Good stories about postmortems and blameless culture; emphasized runbooks and metric-first RCA.

Strengths (headline):
- Strong operational instincts, speaks metric-first and can translate incidents into backlog items.
- Good mental model for cost/latency tradeoffs and autoscaler heuristics.
- Clear communicator for technical debates; uses concrete examples instead of vague platitudes.

Risks / weaknesses: 
- Deep distributed-systems reasoning is solid but sometimes skips edge-case mechanics (e.g., lease expiry under partial partition) — could be OK if we pair/test but important for senior infra role.
- Code hygiene: pragmatic but missed a few defensive patterns; likely fixable in onboarding.
- Question on latched ownership: tends to prefer re-architecting rather than incremental fixes — might be a pro or con depending on squad needs.

Tentative scorecard (1–5 scale) — quick, uncalibrated:
- System design (scale/consistency): 4
- Debugging/incident work: 4
- Latency/cost tradeoffs: 5
- Code quality: 3
- Collaboration / culture fit: 4
- Overall: 4 (lean hire, but want another signal on deep-partition scenarios)

Open follow-ups / suggested checks before final recommend: 
1) Technical take-home: small reproducible test harness that simulates network partitions + lease expiry behavior; ask candidate to provide concrete invariants they would enforce and a short patch/poe to show mitigation approach. Limit to ~4–6 hours.
2) Pairing session: 90m with one of our SRE engineers (Marco) to probe failure modes (split-brain, quorum shifts). Real-time debugging will reveal whether the edge-case skips are conceptual or detail-slips.
3) Ask for a PR/CHANGES snippet from prior role showing how they measured the impact of an autoscaling change (graphs, metrics used, rollout steps). We have a GH PR reference linked above; ask him to point to one specific PR from his past.

Bias checks / calibration notes for panel: 
- He presents confidently; make sure we are not overweighting confidence over eigen-signal. Request concrete artifacts (PRs/metrics) before a hire vote.
- Cultural note: prioritizes reliability and measurable SLOs — aligns well with infra org but could cause friction if paired with very shipping-first product squads.

Decision ask for panel: 
- If Marco + Priya both comfortable after pairing and take-home shows clear thinking on partition edge cases, move to offer. Otherwise, keep warm and re-evaluate in 2 weeks.

My immediate ask (what I'm going to do):
- Send candidate the short take-home today (INFRA-TAKEHOME-01).
- Schedule 90m pairing with Marco for next Tue/Wed window.
- Request 1–2 PR links from Samir (due in 48h).

Quick checklist for SRE pair (short pointers to exercise during pairing):
- Force a single-region majority flip; watch lease renewal cadence and verify invariants.
- Inject delayed heartbeats from a minority of replicas; ask candidate to reason about read-paths and stale-reads exposure.
- Request an incremental mitigation (code/config change) and ask how to roll it out safely with canaries.

Random aside (loggable): candidate used the phrase "observable-first" multiple times — could be a nice culture match for our monitoring-driven iteration.

End of messy dump. Will clean into formal rubric after pairing + take-home.

-- Anika
